stages.title: Getting in
stages.narrator: Congratulations. A stranger has volunteered to drive you through the night. The app says he’s lovely. The app also says the Wi-Fi is free.

panel.alt: 10:40 pm. A yellow ZoomZoom cab brakes to a stop under a streetlight. Through the window, the driver, Ramesh, waves; he is wearing giant sunglasses at night. You stand on the kerb, seen from behind, phone in hand. The app card says: Ramesh, 4.9 stars, ZZ 04 Z 4949, arriving now.

choices.text: Hop in quickly, it’s late and cold.
choices.reaction: Efficient. The plate number is a surprise for later.
choices.label: Hopped straight in

choices.text: Check the plate and driver photo against the app, then get in.
choices.reaction: Look at you, running a background check at 10:40 pm.
choices.label: Checked the plate and photo

choices.text: Photograph the plate and send it to a friend with “Leaving now”.
choices.reaction: A paper trail, delivered in three seconds. Bureaucracy, but make it useful.
choices.label: Sent the plate to a friend

choices.text: Ask the driver “Which name did you get for the booking?” before opening the door.
choices.reaction: Direct, polite, devastatingly efficient. The driver is briefly impressed.
choices.label: Asked him to confirm the booking name

another.why: Matching the plate and photo to the app takes about ten seconds, and it’s the moment you’re most in control.

stages.title: The ride begins
stages.narrator: The trip has begun. So has the small talk.

panel.alt: Inside the cab, from the back seat. Streetlights slide past the windshield. In the rear-view mirror: Ramesh's giant sunglasses. The radio shows FM 98.3. Your phone says 20 minutes to Lakeview Colony.

bubble.speaker: Ramesh
bubble.text: Madam, music? Old songs, new songs?

choices.text: Share the live trip with a friend from the app.
choices.reaction: A friend now has your live location. Your friend is asleep, but still.
choices.label: Shared the live trip

choices.text: Put on headphones and stare out of the window.
choices.reaction: The universal signal for “no thanks”. Unfortunately it also means nobody’s watching the road.
choices.label: Headphones on, eyes on the window

choices.text: Make light conversation to keep things friendly.
choices.reaction: Charming. He now knows your office, your sister’s name and your lunch order.
choices.label: Kept the small talk going

choices.text: Keep the map open on your lap and glance at it now and then.
choices.reaction: Quietly supervising a GPS. A hobby with surprising benefits.
choices.label: Kept the map open

another.why: Trip sharing sends your live route to someone you trust. Being friendly is fine; you just don’t owe anyone your details.

stages.title: The turn that isn’t on the map
stages.narrator: Ten minutes in, the cab turns onto a road your map doesn’t show. The GPS is making a face. You can’t see it, but you can feel it.

panel.alt: The road in the windshield swings away to one side as the cab turns. Close-up of your phone: the blue route goes straight up the main road, but the cab icon turns off onto a dotted side road the map doesn't show. The GPS icon looks unimpressed.

choices.text: Say nothing, he probably knows a shortcut.
choices.reaction: Bold strategy. Let’s see how the shortcut feels about you.
choices.label: Let the shortcut slide

choices.text: Ask calmly, “Is this the usual route? My map shows the main road.”
choices.reaction: A polite question. Also the most inconvenient thing you could do to a bad plan.
choices.label: Asked about the route

choices.text: Call a friend: “Yes, I’m in a cab, tracking it, I’ll reach in ten minutes.”
choices.reaction: Acting skills: unlocked. Everyone in the car is now aware of your friend’s existence.
choices.label: Called a friend, out loud

choices.text: Ask him to stop at the next lit shop because you need water.
choices.reaction: Hydration, the most convincing excuse in history.
choices.label: Asked for a water stop

another.why: A calm question about the route is often enough to bring a driver back to the main road. You’re allowed to ask.

stages.title: The moment of truth
stages.narrator: A lit tea stall ahead. Your phone is at 12%. Plot twist: your battery has joined the story.

panel.alt: Through the cab's side window, the cab slows beside a brightly lit chai stall. The chai-wala pours tea in a long arc; steam rises. Your phone battery reads 12% and is blinking.

choices.text: Keep sitting, the ride will end eventually.
choices.reaction: Patience is a virtue. So is arriving.
choices.label: Waited it out

choices.text: Ask to be dropped at the tea stall and book another cab from there.
choices.reaction: Exiting a bad deal with grace. Economists would be proud.
choices.label: Got out at the tea stall

choices.text: Call the emergency number and stay on the line.
choices.reaction: Not panic. A plan, with backup on speaker.
choices.label: Called the emergency number

choices.text: Message ZoomZoom support through the app.
choices.reaction: Customer service: the unlikely hero of the story. Please hold.
choices.label: Messaged the app’s support

another.why: A busy, well-lit place is a good spot to end a ride that doesn’t feel right. You can always book another.

d.narrator: He pulls over at the lit tea stall for your water. Your phone is at 12%. Plot twist: your battery has joined the story.

good.hint: Want the other ending? Go with the flow this time: hop in, chat, trust the shortcut, sit tight.

variants.title: Chai, Upgraded
variants.alt: You stand at the lit chai stall holding a cup of tea. A new yellow cab pulls in; its card says Lakshmi, 4.97 stars, charger in car, 3 minutes away.
variants.narration: You step out at the tea stall. The chai-wala takes one look at your face and hands you a cutting chai, on the house, “for the drama.” Your next cab arrives in three minutes: Lakshmi, 4.97 stars, phone charger already plugged in. Somewhere behind you, Ramesh is still looking for his shortcut.

variants.title: Dispatch Has Joined the Ride
variants.alt: The cab is back on the main road under the streetlights. Your phone shows a call to 112, on call for 1 minute 42 seconds. A speech bubble: “Passing the big hoarding of the smiling jeweller…”
variants.narration: You stay on the line and describe every landmark like a cricket commentator: “Passing the closed petrol pump. Now the big hoarding of the smiling jeweller.” Ramesh hears all of it. The main road reappears in under a minute. At your gate he asks, very politely, who you were talking to. “A friend,” you say. “A very official one.”

variants.title: The Most Narrated Ride in History
variants.alt: Inside the cab. Ramesh's speech bubbles stack up: “Madam, main road.” “Madam, signal.” “Madam, speed breaker.” “Madam, your gate.”
variants.narration: Two minutes after your message to ZoomZoom support, Ramesh’s phone rings. After that call, he announces every single turn like a tour guide: “Madam, main road. Madam, signal. Madam, speed breaker. Madam, your gate.” You arrive two minutes early. The app asks Ramesh to rate you. Five stars: “Madam very alert. Will not try shortcut again.”

funnyBad.title: Mummy Has Entered the Chat
funnyBad.alt: Your front door at night. Mummy, Papa and the neighbour aunty crowd the doorway holding phones. A family WhatsApp group called “Find Beta” shows messages: CALL ME, I have torch, shared location, bringing samosa. Your phone is dead. A 9 am notification: ₹186 for “route optimisation”.
funnyBad.narration: You reach home 50 minutes late to find Mummy, Papa, the neighbour aunty and a cousin on video call running a WhatsApp group called “Find Beta”, complete with a map and a snacks plan. At 9 am, ZoomZoom charges you ₹186 extra for “route optimisation”.
funnyBad.hint: For a good ending: check the car, share the trip, ask about the route, then pick your exit. There are three different good endings, depending on how you get out.

lead.default: Your phone dies somewhere between the second flyover and a stranger’s baraat.

by.b: You step out at the tea stall, and your phone dies mid-booking. The next cab takes forty minutes and a borrowed charger.
by.c: Your call drops when the battery hits zero, somewhere near a stranger’s baraat. The operator calls back. Your phone does not answer.
by.d: ZoomZoom support replies “We’re looking into it”, and then your phone dies near a stranger’s baraat.

realLife.disclaimer: This was satire. Real situations are messier, faster and scarier than a comic. There is no perfect response, and nothing that happens to you is your fault. These are ideas, not rules.
tips: Before you get in, match the number plate, car and driver photo with the app.
Share your live trip with someone you trust. Most ride apps have a share option and an in-app safety or emergency button; find yours before you need it.
Keep your map open. If the route changes, you’re allowed to ask why.
You can end a ride early at a busy, well-lit place and book another.
Keep some charge for the ride home: a power bank, or a top-up before you leave.
If you feel in danger, call 112, India’s national emergency number.
